doc.title: Howard Mandel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003

title: The critic as consumer guide and mediator; JJA clinics
summary: He wants to be slightly ahead of readers and mediate between musician and reader, and describes JJA clinics for young journalists.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Well a good listener and reader I think could profit from finding a critic or journalist that seems to be on the same wavelength as them, and if they like particular records it’s going to be a good chance that I’m going to enjoy that.

I think the consumer guide aspect of jazz journalism is valuable if it functions in that way. I like to be a little bit ahead of my readers. I hope I can suggest things to them that they haven’t though of before. I mean I want to be — not always provocative or inspiring but I want to be more insightful. I have a lot of experience listening. That’s what I try to do seriously for a living so I hope I can bring something to them they haven’t thought of before. I want to be on the same wavelength with them but I don’t want to hold myself above my reader. And I don’t want to hold myself above the musician who is the creator whose work I’m considering. I want to be a mediator somehow between them. And I think that that means that I have to communicate with the musician either by listening or by actually talking to them. And I need to communicate to my reader by writing clearly and vividly in a way that they enjoy reading, that they’re going to keep reading to get to the end. That’s a writer’s job. So this is something that we try to kind of talk about in the Jazz Journalists Association to some extent. We’re doing clinics today, Thursday, Friday, Saturday with young aspiring jazz journalists and we hope to impart some of the basics of what we’re doing to them, do a little mentoring or guidance for people who are writing, talk to them about the realities of working in jazz journalism, offering them the benefits © Fillius Jazz Archive -16-
